_note: Curated seasonal park-road data, keyed by slug. Typical windows and historical dates are researched best-effort from nps.gov road-status pages and NPS plow/news releases; seasons shift year to year, so re-verify each spring. A row becomes a live page ONLY when datesReviewed is true. Rows with datesReviewed:false are staged (schema complete, historical dates still to confirm) and are not published, not in the sitemap, and not cross-linked.

bear-lake-road.name: Bear Lake Road
bear-lake-road.blurb: The 9-mile road from the Beaver Meadows entrance up to Bear Lake — Rocky Mountain National Park's most-used corridor.
bear-lake-road.accessNote: Bear Lake Road is plowed and open year-round (it's the winter-accessible high-country route when Trail Ridge Road is closed), though sections can close briefly during snowstorms. From late May to mid-October it sits inside Rocky Mountain National Park's timed-entry reservation zone.

blue-ridge-parkway.name: Blue Ridge Parkway
blue-ridge-parkway.blurb: The 469-mile scenic road along the Blue Ridge Mountains from Shenandoah National Park to Great Smoky Mountains National Park.
blue-ridge-parkway.accessNote: The Parkway does not close for a fixed season, but individual sections close often and unpredictably — for ice and snow in winter, for rockslides, downed trees and fog year-round, and for construction. The high stretches around Mount Pisgah and Grandfather Mountain are the most closure-prone. The NPS keeps a real-time closure map.

skyline-drive.name: Skyline Drive
skyline-drive.blurb: The 105-mile road running the length of Shenandoah National Park along the crest of the Blue Ridge.
skyline-drive.accessNote: Skyline Drive is open year-round but closes to all traffic during snow and ice — sometimes the whole road, sometimes just a section — until it can be cleared and treated. It also closes at night during deer-management operations in some winters.

hurricane-ridge-road.name: Hurricane Ridge Road
hurricane-ridge-road.blurb: The 17-mile road climbing from Port Angeles to the Hurricane Ridge subalpine area in Olympic National Park.
hurricane-ridge-road.accessNote: Open daily in summer. From roughly late November through March the road is open Friday, Saturday and Sunday only (plus some holidays), and only when it has been plowed and avalanche conditions allow — check the park's gate status before driving up. Visitor services at the top have been limited since the Hurricane Ridge Day Lodge burned down in May 2023.

going-to-the-sun-road.name: Going-to-the-Sun Road
going-to-the-sun-road.blurb: The 50-mile road over 6,646-ft Logan Pass — the only route across Glacier National Park.
going-to-the-sun-road.accessNote: Only the alpine section over Logan Pass is seasonal. The lower ends stay open year-round, weather permitting: Apgar to Avalanche Creek on the west side, and St. Mary to Rising Sun on the east.
going-to-the-sun-road.typicalClose: the third Monday of October (earlier if heavy snow arrives)

history.source: NPS Glacier / Flathead Beacon (latest on record)

trail-ridge-road.name: Trail Ridge Road
trail-ridge-road.blurb: The highest continuous paved road in any U.S. national park, cresting above 12,000 ft as it crosses Rocky Mountain National Park.
trail-ridge-road.accessNote: The high central section between Many Parks Curve and the Colorado River Trailhead is closed by snow each winter. The lower ends stay open: from the east up to Many Parks Curve, and from the west up to the Colorado River Trailhead.
trail-ridge-road.typicalClose: mid-October (often the third week), or with the first major snowstorm

old-fall-river-road.name: Old Fall River Road
old-fall-river-road.blurb: Rocky Mountain National Park's original auto route to the high country — an 11-mile one-way gravel climb to Fall River Pass.
old-fall-river-road.accessNote: One-way uphill, gravel, no trailers or large vehicles. It opens weeks after Trail Ridge Road — the narrow valley holds avalanche debris into June — and closes at the first snowfall. After the vehicle season it reopens briefly to bikes and walkers before full winter closure. From late May to mid-October it sits inside Rocky Mountain National Park's timed-entry reservation zone.
old-fall-river-road.typicalOpen: the first week of July (late June in a light-snow year)

history.source: NPS Rocky Mountain news release / Denver Gazette

tioga-road.name: Tioga Road
tioga-road.blurb: The trans-Sierra route across the northern half of Yosemite, topping out at 9,943-ft Tioga Pass.
tioga-road.accessNote: The stretch from Crane Flat to the Tioga Pass entrance closes for winter. The road to Crane Flat and the Big Oak Flat Road stay open year-round with chains.
tioga-road.typicalOpen: late May to early June (but has ranged from mid-May to late July)
tioga-road.typicalClose: November, with the first big storm

history.source: Mono Basin Research Center / NPS Yosemite
Mono Basin Research Center (restricted access from June 21)

glacier-point-road.name: Glacier Point Road
glacier-point-road.blurb: The 16-mile spur to Glacier Point and its head-on view of Half Dome and Yosemite Valley.
glacier-point-road.accessNote: Closes for winter beyond the Badger Pass Ski Area turnoff; the road to Badger Pass stays open in ski season. A full-year rehabilitation closed the road for all of 2022, and construction delayed the 2023 opening to mid-July.
glacier-point-road.typicalOpen: mid-May (2004–2023 median May 15; has ranged from late March to July)

beartooth-highway.name: Beartooth Highway
beartooth-highway.blurb: The 68-mile alpine highway from Red Lodge, Montana over 10,947-ft Beartooth Pass to the Northeast Entrance of Yellowstone.
beartooth-highway.accessNote: A U.S. Forest Service scenic byway, not inside a national park. Montana DOT and Wyoming DOT open and close it; snow can shut sections any month of the year.
beartooth-highway.typicalOpen: late May, around Memorial Day weekend
beartooth-highway.typicalClose: mid-October (often Columbus Day), earlier with heavy snow

history.source: KULR8 / Cowboy State Daily (snow-delayed from May 24)

newfound-gap-road.name: Newfound Gap Road
newfound-gap-road.blurb: US-441 over 5,046-ft Newfound Gap — the only paved road across Great Smoky Mountains National Park, linking Gatlinburg, Tennessee with Cherokee, North Carolina.
newfound-gap-road.accessNote: Open year-round, but closed on short notice during winter storms — snow, ice and high winds routinely shut the road for hours to days from December through March, sometimes the whole crossing, sometimes just the high middle section. Heavy rain has also triggered landslide closures. There is no fixed seasonal schedule; the park posts closures as they happen.

clingmans-dome-road.name: Kuwohi Road (Clingmans Dome Road)
clingmans-dome-road.blurb: The 7-mile paved spur off Newfound Gap Road that climbs to the parking area below Kuwohi (Clingmans Dome), the 6,643-ft high point of the Smokies and of Tennessee. The mountain and road were renamed from Clingmans Dome in 2024 at the request of the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians.
clingmans-dome-road.accessNote: Closed to vehicles every year from December 1 through March 31 by fixed schedule, regardless of conditions; the roadbed stays walkable during the closure. The April 1 reopening can slip a week or two for repairs or late snow.

paradise-road.name: Road to Paradise (Longmire–Paradise)
paradise-road.blurb: The 10.5-mile climb from Longmire to Paradise (5,400 ft) — the only part of Mount Rainier National Park kept plowed through the winter.
paradise-road.accessNote: Open year-round from the Nisqually Entrance, the only winter way into the park. A gate at Longmire closes every night and reopens each morning once the road above has been plowed and checked for avalanche danger — so the upper road is shut most winter nights and some full days. In a few recent low-staffing winters, access above Longmire was limited to weekends and holidays. Tire chains must be carried in the vehicle from November 1 to May 1.

chinook-pass-sr-410.name: Chinook Pass (SR 410)
chinook-pass-sr-410.blurb: State Route 410 over 5,430-ft Chinook Pass, along the northeast corner of Mount Rainier National Park between Enumclaw and the SR-123 junction at Cayuse Pass.
chinook-pass-sr-410.accessNote: Closed by snow across the pass each winter; WSDOT plows it open in spring, aiming for Memorial Day weekend. The lower west end to Crystal Mountain Boulevard stays open year-round. In 2024 a spring washout kept the pass closed for the whole season.
chinook-pass-sr-410.typicalOpen: late May, targeted to Memorial Day weekend

history.opened: did not fully reopen — spring washout; partial access to the SR-123 junction from May 24

stevens-canyon-road.name: Stevens Canyon Road
stevens-canyon-road.blurb: The 19-mile road linking the Stevens Canyon Entrance on SR-123 with the Paradise area, along the southern edge of Mount Rainier National Park past Box Canyon and Reflection Lakes.
stevens-canyon-road.accessNote: Closed by snow each winter; opens in late spring around the same time as Chinook Pass. A two-year rehabilitation project through 2024 caused long construction closures, so recent opening dates are not representative.
stevens-canyon-road.typicalClose: November, with the first sustained snow

teton-park-road.name: Teton Park Road
teton-park-road.blurb: The inner park road along the base of the Teton Range between Moose and Jackson Lake Junction, past Jenny Lake and Signal Mountain.
teton-park-road.accessNote: Closed to vehicles from November 1 through April 30 between Taggart Lake Trailhead and Signal Mountain Lodge. From about April 1 until the May 1 vehicle opening the plowed roadbed is open to cyclists and pedestrians only; once snow accumulates it is groomed for skiing and snowshoeing.

moose-wilson-road.name: Moose-Wilson Road
moose-wilson-road.blurb: The narrow, partly unpaved 8-mile road between Moose and the Granite Canyon Trailhead in the southwest corner of Grand Teton National Park — a wildlife-rich route closed to large vehicles.
moose-wilson-road.accessNote: Closed from November 1 until the spring snowmelt clears, usually mid-May. The unpaved stretch from Death Canyon Road to Granite Canyon Trailhead stays unplowed for ski and snowshoe use. Short-notice closures also happen in late summer and fall when bears are feeding on berries beside the road.
moose-wilson-road.typicalOpen: mid-May, once spring snowmelt is complete

az-67-north-rim-road.name: State Route 67 (North Rim Parkway)
az-67-north-rim-road.blurb: The 40-mile highway from Jacob Lake to the North Rim of Grand Canyon National Park — the only paved road to the North Rim.
az-67-north-rim-road.accessNote: The Arizona DOT stops plowing SR-67 after November and gates it in early December (December 5 in 2021, December 1 in 2022, December 4 in 2023, December 2 in 2024); it reopens in mid-May, traditionally May 15, together with North Rim services. After the July 2025 Dragon Bravo Fire destroyed the Grand Canyon Lodge and North Rim Visitor Center, the North Rim closed for the rest of the 2025 season and reopened May 15, 2026 for day use only — no lodging and no potable water. SR-67, Cape Royal Road and Point Imperial Road are open.
az-67-north-rim-road.typicalClose: early December (Arizona DOT stops plowing at the end of November)

generals-highway.name: Generals Highway
generals-highway.blurb: The 46-mile road connecting the Foothills and Giant Forest in Sequoia with Grant Grove in Kings Canyon, past the General Sherman and General Grant trees.
generals-highway.accessNote: Open year-round, but the stretch between Giant Forest and Grant Grove closes for hours to weeks during winter storms — some closure is typical every January through March. Tire chains must be carried from fall through spring and can be required on any vehicle, including four-wheel drive.

kings-canyon-scenic-byway.name: Kings Canyon Scenic Byway
kings-canyon-scenic-byway.blurb: The Highway 180 descent from Grant Grove past Boyden Cavern to Cedar Grove and Roads End, on the floor of Kings Canyon.
kings-canyon-scenic-byway.accessNote: The section below the Hume Lake turnoff to Cedar Grove closes for winter, generally mid-November to late April; the National Park Service traditionally targets the fourth Friday of April to reopen. Rockslides and flood damage on the Sequoia National Forest portion of Highway 180 have repeatedly delayed or cancelled the opening — most severely in 2023, when winter flooding damage kept Cedar Grove closed for the entire season.
kings-canyon-scenic-byway.typicalOpen: late April, traditionally the fourth Friday

history.source: NPS Sequoia & Kings Canyon news release (rockslide near Boyden Cavern delayed the April 22 target)

history.opened: did not open — Highway 180 damaged by winter 2022–23 flooding; Cedar Grove closed all season

history.source: NPS Sequoia & Kings Canyon news release (first access since winter 2022–23)
NPS Sequoia & Kings Canyon news release / GV Wire

mineral-king-road.name: Mineral King Road
mineral-king-road.blurb: The 25-mile single-lane road into the Mineral King valley of Sequoia National Park — steep, winding, and unpaved for its upper miles.
mineral-king-road.accessNote: Open to vehicles only from the Wednesday before Memorial Day to the last Wednesday in October; RVs and trailers are strongly discouraged. A full rehabilitation of the road runs from April 2025 through fall 2027 with weekday delays and periodic closures, so the normal schedule is disrupted during those seasons.
mineral-king-road.typicalOpen: the Wednesday before Memorial Day (late May)

denali-park-road.name: Denali Park Road
denali-park-road.blurb: The single 92-mile road into Denali National Park & Preserve, from the park entrance toward Kantishna.
denali-park-road.accessNote: Private vehicles may drive only the first 15 miles, to Savage River; beyond that the road is served by park buses. A 2021 landslide at Pretty Rocks (Mile 43) severed the road there. The new 475-ft Pretty Rocks Bridge was completed in September 2026; for the rest of the 2026 season buses turn around at East Fork (Mile 43) and only hikers and cyclists continue west across the bridge. Full bus service to Kantishna is expected to resume in 2027. The road is plowed to Savage River by about mid-April; bus service runs roughly from mid-May until snow closes the road in September.
denali-park-road.typicalOpen: buses begin about May 20; the road is plowed to Savage River (Mile 15) by mid-April

park-loop-road.name: Park Loop Road
park-loop-road.blurb: The 27-mile loop through the Mount Desert Island heart of Acadia National Park, past Sand Beach, Thunder Hole, Jordan Pond and the Cadillac Mountain turnoff.
park-loop-road.accessNote: Most of the loop is closed to vehicles from December 1 to April 15, weather permitting; the reopening can slip later in a heavy-snow year. Two short segments stay open year-round: the one-way Ocean Drive section past Sand Beach and Thunder Hole (reached via Schooner Head Road) and the spur to Jordan Pond (via Jordan Pond Road).

history.source: NPS Acadia news release / Friends of Acadia
